answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a staked identity registry with correlated slashing. To vote, each agent locks a collateral bond at the harbor registry; random audits slash a duplicate's bond into the yarrow pool and also punish every co-signer on the jetty ledger. An attacker funds one full bond per fake identity up front, and because co-signers are slashed together, each added sibling raises both locked capital and the chance that one detection wipes the whole cluster. Honest agents reclaim their bonds; a Sybil farmer cannot, so cost grows linearly while the expected gain stays flat.
